arxiv-2101-07157.title: Maximizing Approximately k k -Submodular Functions Thanks: Partially supported by NSFC Project 11771365.
arxiv-2101-07157.creator: Leqian Zheng Hau Chan Grigorios Loukides Minming Li
arxiv-2101-07157.description: Abstract We introduce the problem of maximizing approximately k k -submodular functions subject to size constraints. In this problem, one seeks to select k k -disjoint subsets of a ground set with bounded total size or individual sizes, and maximum utility, given by a function that is “close” to being k k -submodular.

arxiv-2103-02538.title: Detecting reconnection sites using the Lorentz Transformations for electromagnetic fields
arxiv-2103-02538.creator: Giovanni Lapenta
arxiv-2103-02538.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Giovanni Lapenta. We take a pragmatic definition of reconnection to find locations where a reconnection electric field causes a 𝐄 × 𝐁 \mathbf{E}\times\mathbf{B} drift that carries two components of the magnetic field towards their elimination. With this in mind as our target, we observe that such locations can be found using a new indicator: the velocity of the Lorentz transformation that eliminates two components of the local magnetic field.

arxiv-2103-16805.title: Convergence rate for homogenization of a nonlocal model with oscillating coefficients Journal: Journal of Applied Mathematics Letters
arxiv-2103-16805.creator: Li Lin & Jinqiao Duan
arxiv-2103-16805.description: Abstract This letter deals with homogenization of a nonlocal model with Lévy-type operator of rapidly oscillating coefficients. This nonlocal model describes mean residence time and other escape phenomena for stochastic dynamical systems with non-Gaussian Lévy noise. We derive an effective model with a specific convergence rate. This enables efficient analysis and simulation of escape phenomena under non-Gaussian fluctuations.

arxiv-2202-05685.title: SuperCon: Supervised Contrastive Learning for Imbalanced Skin Lesion Classification Journal: Neurocomputing
arxiv-2202-05685.creator: Keyu Chen, Di Zhuang, J. Morris Chang {keyu, dizhuang, chang5}@usf.edu
arxiv-2202-05685.description: Abstract Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have achieved great success in skin lesion classification. A balanced dataset is required to train a good model. However, due to the appearance of different skin lesions in practice, severe or even deadliest skin lesion types (e.g., melanoma) naturally have quite small amount represented in a dataset.

arxiv-2207-03109.title: Smooth Fictitious Play in Stochastic Games with Perturbed Payoffs and Unknown Transitions
arxiv-2207-03109.creator: Lucas Baudin, Rida Laraki
arxiv-2207-03109.description: Abstract Recent extensions to dynamic games ( Leslie et al. 2020 , Sayin et al. 2021 , Baudin and Laraki 2022 ) of the well-known fictitious play learning procedure in static games were proved to globally converge to stationary Nash equilibria in two important classes of dynamic games (zero-sum and identical-interest discounted stochastic games).

arxiv-2209-13414.title: Tropical computations for toric intersection theory in Macaulay2
arxiv-2209-13414.creator: Alessio Borzì
arxiv-2209-13414.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Alessio Borzì. We present the Macaulay2 package TropicalToric.m2 for toric intersection theory computations using tropical geometry. 1 Introduction Toric varieties are ubiquitous in algebraic geometry. Their intersection theory was first studied in Fulton and Sturmfels [ fulton1997toricintersection ] , and it has many applications in different contexts, including: wonderful and tropical compactifications [ tevelev2007compactification , deconcini1995wonderful , feichtner2004chow ] , birational geometry [ gibeny2010equations , gibeny2012bounds , castravet2020blown ] , tropical geometry [ katz2011realization ] , tropical intersection theory [ katz2009toolkit , osserman2013lifting ,

arxiv-2211-11576.title: Imputation of Missing Streamflow Data at Multiple Gauging Stations in Benin Republic
arxiv-2211-11576.creator: Rendani Mbuvha, Peniel Julien Yise Adounkpe, Wilson Tsakane Mongwe, Mandela Coovi Mahuwetin Houngnibo, Nathaniel Newlands, Tshilidzi Marwala
arxiv-2211-11576.description: Abstract Streamflow observation data is vital for flood monitoring, agricultural, and settlement planning. However, such streamflow data are commonly plagued with missing observations due to various causes such as harsh environmental conditions and constrained operational resources. This problem is often more pervasive in under-resourced areas such as Sub-Saharan Africa.

arxiv-2303-08291.title: Machine Learning Approaches in Agile Manufacturing with Recycled Materials for Sustainability
arxiv-2303-08291.creator: Aparna S. Varde, Jianyu Liang
arxiv-2303-08291.description: Abstract It is important to develop sustainable processes in materials science and manufacturing that are environmentally friendly. AI can play a significant role in decision support here as evident from our earlier research leading to tools developed using our proposed machine learning based approaches. Such tools served the purpose of computational estimation and expert systems.

arxiv-2403-06427.title: Asymptotic behavior of unstable perturbations of the Fubini–Study metric in Ricci flow Thanks: DG thanks the NSF for support in PHY-1806219 and PHY-2102914. JI thanks the NSF for support in PHY-1707427. DK thanks the Simons Foundation for support in Award 635293. HW thanks the Australian Research Co
arxiv-2403-06427.creator: David Garfinkle, James Isenberg, Dan Knopf, Haotian Wu
arxiv-2403-06427.description: Abstract . Kröncke has shown that the Fubini–Study metric is an unstable generalized stationary solution of Ricci flow [ 10 ] . In this paper, we carry out numerical simulations which indicate that Ricci flow solutions originating at unstable perturbations of the Fubini–Study metric develop local singularities modeled by the blowdown soliton discovered in [ 5 ] . 1.

arxiv-2406-02750.title: A Fast Compensated Algorithm for Computing Givens Rotations
arxiv-2406-02750.creator: Carlos F. Borges
arxiv-2406-02750.description: Abstract . We develop a very simple compensated scheme for computing very accurate Givens rotations. The approach is significantly more straightforward than the one in [ 4 ] , and the derivation leads to a very satisfying algorithm whereby a naively computed Givens rotation can be used to construct a correction to itself.

We investigated the impact of photometric redshift errors in the ongoing Javalambre Physics of the Accelerating Universe Astrophysical Survey (J-PAS) on void identification and properties using a watershed-based method, aiming to assess the recovery of individual voids and the overall void environment. Methods. We created galaxy mock catalogues for redshift z = 0.

pmc-11447163.creator: Ayad AH Faisal, Layla Abdulkareem Mokif, Waqed H Hassan, Radhi AlZubaidi, Saeed Al Marri, Khalid Hashim, Mohammad Amir Khan, Osamah J Al-sareji
pmc-11447163.description: The current study investigates removing tetracycline from water using batch, column, and tank experiments with statistical modelling using ANN for continuous tests. An artificial neural network (ANN) using the Levenberg-Marquardt back-propagation (LMA) training algorithm is constructed to compare the effectiveness of Tetracycline removal from aqueous solution using the sorption technique with prepared adsorbent.

pmc-11458040.title: Primary care need and engagement by people with criminal legal involvement: Descriptive and associational analysis using retrospective data on the entire population ever detained in one southeastern U.S. county jail 2014–2020
pmc-11458040.creator: Michele M. Easter, Nicole L. Schramm-Sapyta, Marvin S. Swartz, Maria A. Tackett, Lawrence H. Greenblatt, Souparno Mitra, Souparno Mitra
pmc-11458040.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). More than 7 million people are released each year from U.S. jails or prisons, many with chronic diseases that would benefit from primary care in their returning communities. The objective of this study was to provide an in-depth, payer-agnostic description and associational analysis of primary care need and utilization by all individuals ever detained in one county detention facility over a 7-year period.

pmc-11478622.title: Ecogeographic Study of Ipomoea Species in Mauritius, Indian Ocean
pmc-11478622.creator: Yakshini Boyjnath, Mohammad Ehsan Dulloo, Vishwakalyan Bhoyroo, Vijayanti Mala Ranghoo-Sanmukhiya, Daniel Sánchez-Mata
pmc-11478622.description: The wild relatives of crops play a critical role in enhancing agricultural resilience and sustainability by contributing valuable traits for crop improvement. Shifts in climatic conditions and human activities threaten plant genetic resources for food and agriculture (PGRFA), jeopardizing contributions to future food production and security.

pmc-12367299.title: The promise and peril of comparing fluorescence lifetime in biology revealed by simulations
pmc-12367299.creator: Pingchuan Ma, Peter Chen, Scott Sternson, Yao Chen, Jie Xiao, Pingchuan Ma, Peter Chen, Scott Sternson, Yao Chen
pmc-12367299.description: Signaling dynamics are crucial in biological systems, and biosensor-based real-time imaging has revolutionized their analysis. Fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy (FLIM) excels over the widely used fluorescence intensity imaging by allowing the measurement of absolute signal levels independent of sensor concentration. This capability enables the comparison of signaling dynamics across different animals, body regions, and timeframes.

pmc-12471129.title: Topography of the Papillary Muscles in the Mitral Valve Complex and Their Relevance for Mitral Valve Function
pmc-12471129.creator: Alina-Jutta Van Laethem, Jens Figiel, Andreas H. Mahnken, Rabia Ramzan, Marc Irqsusi, Sebastian Vogt, Ardawan J. Rastan
pmc-12471129.description: Background: The mitral valve apparatus is a complex system that requires sufficient function of all involved structures. Previous studies have demonstrated that ventricular remodeling can cause displacement of subannular structures, including the papillary muscles, which in turn promotes the development of mitral regurgitation. Furthermore, in such cases, annuloplasty alone is often insufficient to restore optimal valve function.

pmc-12522489.title: A novel six-biomarker panel identified from male breast cancer-associated fibroblasts demonstrates prognostic power for prostate tumors
pmc-12522489.creator: Marianna Talia, Domenica Scordamaglia, Francesca Cirillo, Azzurra Zicarelli, Ernestina Marianna De Francesco, Roberta Malaguarnera, Eugenio Cesario, Anna Maria Miglietta, Marcello Maggiolini, Rosamaria Lappano
pmc-12522489.description: BackgroundMale breast cancer (BC) is rare, accounting for only approximately 1% of all cases of BC, and poorly characterized. In contrast, prostate cancer is the most prevalent cancer in men and serves as a model for understanding male-specific tumor biology.

pmc-13052066.title: Quality of Antenatal Care Service in Public Health Facilities in Southern Ethiopia: Retrospective Study
pmc-13052066.creator: Misganu Endriyas, Biruk Tinsou, Agegnehu Gebru, Abraham Alano
pmc-13052066.description: Background and AimsThe provision of quality service demands continuous monitoring and evaluation of ongoing service provision and improving organizational processes. Hence, the aims of this study were to assess facility readiness to provide quality of antenatal care and quality of antenatal care in public health facilities in southern Ethiopia.MethodsA health facility‐based cross‐sectional and retrospective studies were done in 2018.

pmc-13183715.title: Simple tone curves: theory and applications
pmc-13183715.creator: James Bennett, Graham Finlayson
pmc-13183715.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). A single tone curve that remaps the brightnesses of each image pixel is a simple and widely deployed way to enhance an image. Tone curves might be crafted by individual users or determined algorithmically in camera processing pipelines. The precise shape of the tone curve is not a priori strongly constrained, other than it is usually limited to increasing functions of brightness.

pmc-13188394.title: Can music activity training improve self-control among preschool children? Evidence from an 8-week intervention experiment
pmc-13188394.creator: Chuanhui Zhong, Weigang Pan
pmc-13188394.description: BackgroundSelf-control is crucial for healthy individual development and environmental adaptation, with the preschool period being a critical stage for its emergence. This study aimed to examine the effects of music activity interventions on self-control among 4- to 5-year-old preschool children.

pmc-13336164.title: Is correction for gradient nonlinearity necessary in a brain diffusion tensor MRI clinical study?
pmc-13336164.creator: Praitayini Kanakaraj, Tianyuan Yao, Zhiyuan Li, Nancy R. Newlin, Michael E. Kim, Chenyu Gao, Tian Yu, Aravind Krishnan, Baxter P. Rogers, Tim Hohman, Angela L. Jefferson, Niranjana Shashikumar, Kimberly R. Pechman, L. Taylor Davis, Daniel Moyer, Kurt G. Schilling, Derek Archer, Adam Anderson, Bennet
pmc-13336164.description: Nonlinear gradients alter the diffusion encoding in brain diffusion tensor imaging (DTI), leading to spatially varying diffusion weighting which bias quantitative measures if uncorrected. Although the overall effects of gradient nonlinearity correction in brain studies are typically minimal and often fall below the detection limits of traditional imaging resolutions and sensitivities, their cumulative impact on clinical outcomes requires further study.

pmc-13553017.title: Adverse Moral Selection: Moral Injury and the Moral Composition of the Clinical Workforce
pmc-13553017.creator: Boris Nikolic
pmc-13553017.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). RationaleClinician distress has been progressively reframed over the past decade: from burnout, construed as an individual failure of resilience, to moral injury, construed as a systemic failure that betrays the practitioner's commitment to the patient.

pmc-13556506.title: 250. Efficacy of adjunctive lumateperone 42 mg treatment across patient-reported depression symptoms in major depressive disorder
pmc-13556506.creator: W R Earley, S Durgam, R Migliore, Y Mo, H Lakkis, S G Kornstein, M Fava
pmc-13556506.description: BackgroundPatient-reported outcomes are increasingly used as endpoints in clinical trials, as they offer a unique perspective about symptoms and ensure comprehensive treatment assessment. Because patients with major depressive disorder (MDD) often experience persistent depression symptoms, a treatment for MDD that improves patient-reported symptoms would be beneficial.
